method: Supporting indicators (inventories-to-sales, weekly hours, real consumer spending, payroll revisions) are shown for context and are not part of the scores yet. Each indicator scores +1 / 0 / −1 (stress 0 to +1). Growth, inflation and stress are the averages. Growth ≤ −0.25 = slowdown; inflation ≥ +0.34 = late cycle; growth ≥ +0.25 = mid-cycle; in between, early recovery if claims are falling and the curve is steepening. Data: FRED, St. Louis Fed. Swing filters (Baumohl): sentiment vs. real retail sales (UMich, FRED), Fed Beige Book keyword counts vs. two reports earlier, freight (Cass shipments, ATA truck tonnage, BDRY dry-bulk ETF) and yield-curve steepening after inversion. Each active filter makes setups on its side easier (minimum score −1) and the other side harder (+1), from a base of 6.

filters.name: Sentiment vs. spending
filters.text: Sentiment 55.2 → 48.1 over 2 months; real retail sales +0.5% over 3 months. Mood is sinking while spending holds up: likely debt-financed. Watch for distribution tops in ES/NQ.

filters.name: Fed Beige Book tone
filters.text: Hawkish phrases 48 (-14% vs. 202607), dovish 30 (+30%), per 10k words. Slack language (layoffs, discounting, caution) is rising fast: long bias on bond futures.
filters.detail: Most frequent: hawkish price increases 28, wage pressures 11, shortages 7; dovish slowing demand 11, layoffs 7, cautious outlook 7.

filters.name: Freight and shipping
filters.text: Cass shipments +1.9% y/y; truck tonnage -2.4% over 3 months; dry-bulk shipping (BDRY) -17% over 45 trading days. No sustained break.

filters.name: Yield curve
filters.text: 10y − 2y = +0.38; over 3 months the 2-year moved +0.44 and the 10-year +0.38. Not recently inverted.
